# Enhanced MuleSoft Experience Release Notes

> For the full documentation index, see: https://docs.mulesoft.com/llms.txt

The enhanced MuleSoft experience is a unified workspace for managing, governing, and monitoring
AI-connected integration assets, including agents, APIs, Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, model
proxies, and gateways. Teams use it to register services, apply governance strategies, monitor
runtime health, and optimize costs from one portfolio view instead of working across disconnected
tools.

## August 6, 2026

### What’s New

#### Features

- Playgrounds are now available for APIs and MCP servers. Use the **Playground** tab on a service
  detail page to explore endpoints and tools, configure and send requests, and inspect responses
  without leaving the enhanced experience.

  For more information, see
  [Testing Services with Playgrounds](../../general/exp-playground-overview),
  [Testing APIs in the API Playground](../../general/exp-playground-api), and
  [Exploring MCP Server Tools in the MCP Playground](../../general/exp-playground-mcp).

- The Akamai scanner is now available to map external security findings to the right services in
  **Portfolio**. Add the scanner to scan APIs, surface security findings, and apply governance
  strategies from the portfolio. The scanner doesn’t import or register third-party services. It
  correlates risk scores, findings, and incidents in one governance workflow.

  For more information, see
  [Correlating Risk Using Akamai API Security](../../general/exp-akamai-risk-correlation) and
  [Working with Governance Strategies](../../general/exp-governance-work-with-strategies).

- Additional Trusted MCP server SaaS integrations are now available, and ready-to-use MCP client
  configuration snippets help you connect popular MCP clients faster.

- Model Proxy now supports the Anthropic API format and native Anthropic models.

  See [Supported LLM Providers](../../general/model-proxy#supported-llm-providers).

- API scanners now read policies from these provider platforms: Amazon API Gateway, Google Apigee,
  Azure API Management, and Kong Gateway. For these providers, policy results are visible from each
  discovered API in **Portfolio** > **APIs** > **Policies**.

  After connecting to a third-party API gateway provider, you can govern discovered APIs through the
  same governance workflow used for Anypoint Platform APIs. This enables unified governance across
  multiple gateway platforms.

  For more information, see:

  - [Adding Scanners from Providers](../../general/exp-scanners-add-from-providers)

  - [Viewing Service Details in the Portfolio](../../general/exp-services-view-details)

  - [Create Governance Strategies with Your IDE](../../general/exp-governance-create-strategy#create-with-ide)

  - [Govern Third-Party Provider APIs](../../general/exp-governance-govern-third-party-apis)

  - [Monitoring Cross-Gateway Conformance](../../general/exp-governance-monitor-cross-gateway-conformance)

#### Enhancements

- The Scanner details page now includes an Activity Log with a real-time timeline of scan progress
  events.

  For more information, see
  [Viewing Scanner History and Settings](../../general/exp-scanners-view-details).

- MCP Bridge now lets you edit tool input schemas, customize tool HTTP request mappings and headers,
  and expose tool output schemas as part of the MCP specification.

- Cost Management now lets you edit optimization policies and is available from the Ask MuleSoft
  sidebar.

- The LLM proxy credential test now distinguishes between credentials that can’t be verified and
  credentials that are invalid.

- LLM Proxy is now renamed to Model Proxy.

## July 15, 2026

### What’s New

#### Features

- The new Payload Optimization policy page lets you configure token-reduction strategies, including
  payload sanitization and TOON encoding, as toggleable sub-policies.

- Cost Management now surfaces Payload Optimization sub-policies as opportunity cards, so you can
  act on top token-savings recommendations directly from the Cost Management page.

- The new MCP Tools Progressive Disclosure policy enables you to reduce context window token cost by
  exposing tools on demand through search. Apply the policy Cost Management.

- Instance detail pages now display the consumer endpoint URL, including the base path, so you can
  copy a callable URL without switching to Anypoint Platform.

#### Enhancements

- Tool Mapping policy configuration now includes a version selector, so you can update the policy to
  a new version.

- Applied policies now display a "New version available" indicator when a newer version is
  available.

- The model proxy overview now shows the configured fallback route and semantic prompt guard as
  summary cards, so you can review them without entering edit mode.

## June 22, 2026

### What’s New

#### Enhancements

- Notifications are now available, allowing you to configure and receive alerts for service health
  and governance events.

  For more information, see
  [Configuring Notifications for Alerts](../../general/exp-alerts-configure-notifications).

- MuleSoft Agent is now available. Manage your MuleSoft environment with MuleSoft Agent, an agentic
  experience available in the control plane. Use MuleSoft Agent to create scanners, apply policies,
  deploy instances, and perform other management tasks. To request access, contact your account
  executive.

  For more information, see [Using the MuleSoft Agent](../../general/exp-ai-assistant-use).

- MuleSoft for Slack is now available. Install the MuleSoft Slack app to interact with the MuleSoft
  Platform directly from your Slack workspace, send platform notifications to Slack channels or
  direct messages, take platform actions, and ask questions about your MuleSoft organization.

  For more information, see
  [Integrate the Enhanced Experience with Slack](../../general/exp-slack-integrate).

## May 28, 2026

### What’s New

- You can now manage agents, APIs, MCP servers, model proxies, and gateways from one portfolio
  experience, so teams can govern and operate AI integrations without switching between separate
  tools.

  For more information, see [Enhanced MuleSoft Experience](../../general/learning-map-exp) and
  [Enhanced MuleSoft Experience Overview](../../general/exp-overview).

- You can now add services through provider-based discovery or manual registration, so teams can
  onboard both cloud-managed and custom services faster.

  For more information, see
  [Adding Services to Your Portfolio](../../general/exp-services-add-to-portfolio),
  [Create a Scanner for Provider Services](../../general/exp-services-connect-providers-to-add), and
  [Register Services Manually](../../general/exp-services-register-manually).

- You can now create MCP servers by selecting source systems and publishing tools and resources for
  MCP clients, so you can more easily expose existing APIs and SaaS systems through MCP workflows.

  For more information, see [Create MCP Servers](../../general/exp-services-create-mcp-server).

- You can now add semantic services with Basic and Advanced scale models, so LLM-driven requests
  route with improved context awareness as traffic grows.

  For more information, see
  [Configuring Semantic Services](../../general/model-proxy-semantic-service).

- You can now apply governance strategies across supported service types, so teams can enforce
  conformance and cost controls more consistently.

  For more information, see
  [Create Governance Strategies](../../general/exp-governance-create-strategy) and
  [Viewing Service Details in the Portfolio](../../general/exp-services-view-details).

- Scanner operations now support lifecycle workflows for running, pausing, editing, and deleting
  scanners, so provider discovery stays current with less manual overhead.

  For more information, see
  [Adding Scanners from Providers](../../general/exp-scanners-add-from-providers) and
  [Running and Managing Scanners](../../general/exp-scanners-manage).

- Service detail pages now centralize instance creation and management workflows for supported
  catalogs, so teams can align deployment operations with governance and monitoring workflows.

  For more information, see
  [Creating and Managing Instances of Services](../../general/exp-instances-add) and
  [Viewing Service Details in the Portfolio](../../general/exp-services-view-details).

- Monitoring guidance now connects service health, detailed metrics, and token and response
  analysis, so responders can triage regressions faster.

  For more information, see
  [Monitoring Services in Your Portfolio](../../general/exp-services-monitoring),
  [View Detailed Metrics for Your Services](../../general/exp-services-view-detailed-metrics), and
  [Managing Costs and Token Usage](../../general/exp-governance-view-cost-and-token-usage).

- You can now access the experience from Anypoint Platform, direct URLs, and supported coding
  assistants, so teams can work from existing workflow surfaces.

  For more information, see [Get Started with the Enhanced Experience](../../general/exp-home-start)
  [Connect the Enhanced Experience to Claude Desktop](../../general/exp-claude-desktop-connect).

- Service detail pages now clarify tab availability by service type, so operators can more easily
  find instance, governance, and conformance data by catalog.

  For more information, see
  [Viewing Service Details in the Portfolio](../../general/exp-services-view-details).

# Anypoint Platform EU Control Plane Release Notes: December 15, 2017

> For the full documentation index, see: https://docs.mulesoft.com/llms.txt

This document describes new features and enhancements, known limitations, issues, and fixes in EU
control plane.

## New Features and Enhancements

Beginning on December 15, 2017 the Anypoint Platform control plane is available in the European
Union.

This release includes the following new features and enhancements:

- EU control plane deployed in EU

- Runtime Manager supports deploying to applications to CloudHub hosted in the EU.

- The `amc_setup` command supports `eu1` as value of the `region` option. This enables you to
  connect a customer-managed Mule runtime to the EU control plane.

- Mule runtime includes changes to the `wrapper.conf` file and the command line that support
  connecting to the EU control plane.

- Support for Object Store v2.

## Changes in This Release

There are no changes in this release.

## Fixed Issues

There are no fixed issues in this release.

## Known Limitations and Workarounds

This section lists known limitations and workarounds for this release.

- Public exchange is not fully supported in this release. Although certain public assets are
  available in the EU control plane, the full set of public assets are not available.

  To take advantage of assets available in the public Exchange of the US control plane, copy those
  assets to a private Exchange within the EU control plane. Private Exchange is fully supported in
  the EU control plane.

- When deploying to CloudHub, you can only deploy applications and gateways to the Frankfurt region.
  Additionally, the number of supported Mule runtime versions is smaller.

- Object Store v1 is not supported.

- Anypoint Platform users must create a separate account to access the EU control plane.

- You can only create dedicated load balancers and virtual private clouds (VPCs) in the Frankfurt
  region. The suffix for the external domain names of dedicated load balancers on the EU control
  plane is `lb-prod-eu-rt.anypointdns.net`.

- Migration between regions is a manual process. You must manually copy each asset from the US
  control to the EU control plane.

## Upgrade Requirements

There are no upgrade requirements in this release.

## Compatibility Notes

- CloudHub

  When deploying an application to CloudHub in the EU control plane, only the following versions of
  the Mule runtime are supported:

  - 3.8.5 or later

  - 3.9.0 or later

  - 4.0.0 or later

  - API Gateway 2.2.0

- Customer-managed Mule Runtimes (Hybrid)

  When deploying to a customer-managed runtime, Mule runtime version 3.x is supported as long as you
  are using Mule Runtime Manager Agent, version 1.9.2. This version is bundled with Mule runtime,
  version 3.8.x and later. To use earlier versions of Mule runtime, you must download version 3.8.x
  and install version 1.9.2 of the Runtime Manager Agent in your environment.

- Anypoint Studio

  Anypoint Studio versions 6.4.2 and 7.0.1 support the Anypoint Platform EU control plane.

# Anypoint Exchange Release Notes

> For the full documentation index, see: https://docs.mulesoft.com/llms.txt

Anypoint Exchange is a curated catalog of reusable assets such as agents, APIs, API groups, API spec
fragments, brokers, custom assets, examples, large language models (LLMs), Model Context Protocol
(MCP) servers, policies, templates, integration assets such as connectors. You can catalog
(publish), share, discover, learn about, and reuse assets within your organization to facilitate
collaboration, boost productivity, and promote standards.

## August 6, 2026

### What’s New

- API scanners now read policies from these provider platforms: Amazon API Gateway, Google Apigee,
  Azure API Management, and Kong Gateway.

  For more information, see:

  - [Adding a Scanner for Amazon API Gateway](../../exchange/adding-amazon-gateway-scanner)

  - [Adding a Scanner for Google Apigee](../../exchange/adding-apigee-scanner)

  - [Adding a Scanner for Azure API Management](../../exchange/adding-azure-api-management-scanner)

  - [Adding a Scanner for Kong Gateway](../../exchange/adding-kong-gateway-scanner)

## July 2026

### What’s New

- Publishing custom connectors and Mule plugins to Exchange now requires Java compatibility metadata
  in `mule-artifact.json` for new versions that change supported Java compatibility.

  To avoid publishing failures, update your connector build configuration to a supported supported
  Mule SDK or plugin configuration that writes Java compatibility metadata before publishing new
  versions.

  This change doesn’t affect connectors already published to Exchange or running applications.

  For configuration steps and troubleshooting, see
  [Publishing Connectors to Exchange](../../mule-sdk/latest/publishing-connectors-exchange).

- Exchange now supports publishing A2A Protocol v1.0 agent cards. When you create an agent asset,
  you can select **A2A v1.0 card** as the protocol type to publish a v1.0-compliant Agent Card. The
  v1.0 card supports the `supportedInterfaces` field for declaring transport bindings and optional
  card signatures.

  A2A v0.3 cards remain available as a separate protocol option (**A2A v0.3 card**). A single asset
  version can carry both a v0.3 card and a v1.0 card under separate classifiers. There is no
  automatic conversion between versions.

  For more information, see [Create an Agent](../../exchange/to-create-an-asset#create-agent).

- The card details page for A2A v1.0 agents now displays:

  - Supported interfaces (protocol binding, URL, protocol version, and tenant)

  - Signature indicator (shown only for signed cards)

  - Provider information

  - Security schemes

  - Capabilities (streaming, push notifications, state transition history)

  - Skills (with descriptions, input/output modes, and examples)

- Exchange now includes Agent Network as a supported asset type. An agent network is a coordinated
  group of agents, brokers, LLMs, and MCP servers that acts as a central hub for defining,
  validating, and executing agentic processes across your enterprise. This asset is published to
  Exchange from Anypoint Code Builder and is read-only.

  For more information, see [Asset Types](../../exchange/asset-types).

- You can now use the Agentforce scanner to import Agentforce agents into Exchange.

  For more information, see
  [Adding a Scanner for Salesforce Agentforce Agents](../../exchange/adding-agentforce-scanner).

- You can now add scanners to automatically discover and catalog MCP servers from these external
  providers:

  - Microsoft Azure API Management MCP Server

  - Databricks Agent Bricks MCP Server

    For more information, see:

    - [Adding a Scanner for Salesforce Agentforce Agents](../../exchange/adding-agentforce-scanner)

    - [Adding a Scanner for Azure API Management MCP Server](../../exchange/adding-azure-apim-mcp-scanner)

    - [Adding a Scanner for Databricks MCP Server](../../exchange/adding-databricks-mcp-scanner)

- The Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime scanner now adds richer metadata to Exchange agent cards and
  documentation, helping users evaluate agents faster.

  The Exchange details page for scanned agents now shows:

  - Created At

  - Updated At

  - Foundation Model

  - Skills

  - Collaboration Model

- Importing Agentforce agents from **Settings** is deprecated. To import Agentforce agents, create
  an Agentforce scanner.

  For more information, see
  [Adding a Scanner for Salesforce Agentforce Agents](../../exchange/adding-agentforce-scanner).

## May 2026

### What’s New

- Generative AI documentation now supports gRPC APIs, MCP servers, and agents, in addition to REST,
  SOAP, AsyncAPI, and GraphQL APIs.

  For more information, see
  [Generating API Documentation with Generative AI](../../exchange/generating-documentation-with-ai).

- You can now add a scanner to discover, import, and sync APIs from external providers into
  Exchange. Once imported, you can apply governance rulesets and publish these services to a
  developer portal. Supported gateways are Amazon API Gateway, Azure API Management, Kong API
  Gateway, and Google Apigee.

  For more information, see:

  - [Adding a Scanner for Amazon API Gateway](../../exchange/adding-amazon-gateway-scanner)

  - [Adding a Scanner for Azure API Management](../../exchange/adding-azure-api-management-scanner)

  - [Adding a Scanner for Kong Gateway](../../exchange/adding-kong-gateway-scanner)

  - [Adding a Scanner for Google Apigee](../../exchange/adding-apigee-scanner)

- The Amazon AgentCore scanner has been enhanced to now support the automatic discovery and
  cataloging of MCP servers. After the MCP servers are registered, you can govern and consume them
  in other applications.

  For more information, see
  [Adding a Scanner for Amazon Bedrock AgentCore MCP](../../exchange/adding-agentcore-mcp-scanner).

- You can now review and approve scan results before they’re imported into Exchange, giving you
  control over which external services are added to your catalog. When you configure a scanner to
  **Ask to review**, its status changes to **Pending review** after the scan completes. Open the
  scan to choose which services to import. Services you don’t import remain pending and reappear in
  the next scan. To permanently exclude a service from future scans, use the action menu to add it
  to the **Skipped** list.

  To enable manual review, set the scheduled run configuration to **Ask to review** when you add or
  edit a scanner.

  For more information, see
  [Review Scan Results Manually](../../exchange/managing-scanners#review-scan-results-manually).

- The **Agent Scanners** page in the Exchange sidebar has been renamed to Scanners, where you can
  now access all scanners regardless of service type from a single page.

  For more information, see
  [Discovering and Cataloging External Services with Scanners](../../exchange/discovering-and-importing-external-agents).

### What’s New

- You can now add agent scanners to automatically discover and register AI agents across agent

  Azure Copilot. After the agents are registered, govern and consume them in other applications.

  For more information, see
  [Discovering and Cataloging External Services with Scanners](../../exchange/discovering-and-importing-external-agents).

- You can now use an MCP server URL to add the server’s metadata when publishing it to the registry
  in Exchange.

  For more information, see [Create an MCP Server](../../exchange/to-create-an-asset#create-mcp).

- Exchange now syncs public MCP servers from the official MCP registry to **Provided by MuleSoft**.

  These public MCP servers are maintained by the original providers and not MuleSoft.

- You can now create and manage instances for publicly available MCP servers in API Manager to
  govern and monitor public assets.

  These assets are published to Exchange under **Provided by MuleSoft** and are maintained by their
  original providers, not by MuleSoft. When you create an instance from a publicly available asset,
  the instance is created within your private organization in Exchange and managed like any other
  instance in API Manager.

  For more information see,
  [Adding an MCP Server from Public Exchange](../../api-manager/latest/create-instance-public-exchange).

- You can now request access to running instances from publicly available assets. Instances for MCP
  servers published in **Provided by MuleSoft** are created within your private organization.

## July 2025

### What’s New

- Admins can choose how asset owners can dte asset versions in Exchange. They can enable or disable
  the ability to permanently delete an asset to reuse the GAV (group ID, asset ID, and version) for
  a new asset. It doesn’t matter when the asset version was created. When enabled, asset owners see
  an option to allow the GAV to be reused when deleting an asset version. When disabled, the GAV
  can’t be reused after deleting the asset version.

  For more information, see [Managing Asset Deletion](../../exchange/managing-asset-deletion).

- Admins can control whether or not to assign owner roles when creating assets using a connected
  app. When enabled, when creating new assets using a connected app, roles aren’t assigned to
  connected app owners. When disabled, roles are assigned by default.

  For more information, see [Managing Connected Apps](../../exchange/managing-connected-apps).

  For more information, see
  [Generating API Documentation with Generative AI](../../exchange/generating-documentation-with-ai).

- Client application owners can now add multiple individual users or teams as additional owners,

  For more information, see

## October 2023

### What’s New

You can now find and discover assets using the **Custom field** filter in the enhanced search

## July 2023

### What’s New

Exchange now provides asset usage and engagement metrics for administrators and asset owners to gain
insight into the consumption and user engagement of their API specification fragments and REST APIs.
The usage metrics measure how many times those assets are downloaded from Exchange, imported from
API Designer, imported from Anypoint Studio, and the number of dependents and contracts for the
asset. The asset engagement score is a composite metric that administrators and asset owners can use
to measure the usage of the assets in Exchange.

## May 2023

### What’s New

The assets details page lets you find specific information within the API specification and pages of
an asset using the CTRL+F or the command+F keyboard shortcut. In Exchange, this enhanced shortcut
overrides the native browser shortcut, which searches only for words and phrases on the current
page.

## April 2023

### What’s New

Exchange now includes the following RPA template asset types:

- RPA Activity templates

  Activity templates are reusable code within RPA to standardize the most used activity steps and
  make them available to other developers in the organization. These templates are `.cawl` files
  that are imported in the RPA Activity library for developers to use as part of their RPA
  processes.

- RPA Process templates

  Templates for RPA processes are imported into RPA Builder as projects and are customizable before
  deploying to RPA bots. Process templates are built on common patterns for RPA to build automation
  faster. These templates are `.crpa` files that are exported from RPA Builder to share with other
  developers.

## February 2023

### What’s New

- The enhanced search is now the default search experience for users logging into Exchange.

  Using the enhanced experience, you can:

  - Filter assets by type, organization, category, tag, and lifecycle state

  - See which API Spec properties and page text matched the search term

  - Save shortcuts to filters you have applied

  - Sort search results by relevance, name, last modified date, or rating  
    For more details about the enhanced search, see
    [Search for Assets](../../exchange/to-find-info).

    The legacy search experience is still available by clicking **Back to legacy search** from the
    Exchange landing page.

- Exchange now supports JSON Schema and OAS 3.0 components as sub-types for the API Fragments asset
  type.

## January 2023

### What’s New

- The product now uses more inclusive language.

- Exchange now includes the GraphQL API asset type.

  A GraphQL API allows a client to fetch only the object types and fields needed instead of fetching
  a fixed response like in a REST API.

- A new Creator permission gives users the Asset Administrator role for the assets they create but
  restricts modifying assets or asset versions created by other users in the business group. For

## April 2022

### What’s New

Exchange now includes the following asset types:

- Policy definition - Policies enforce regulations to help manage security, control traffic, and
  improve API adoption. Create a policy definition based on your specific business requirements and
  apply them to APIs to extend existing functionality or define new ones.

- Ruleset - Rulesets are a group of rules or guidelines that define an application, for example,
  best practices or industry-specific standards. Add a ZIP file with multiple YAML files that
  describe the new ruleset.

## March 2022

### New Features

Exchange now supports asset lifecycle states of development, stable, and deprecated to track the
progress of assets as they move through the software development lifecycle.

We intuitively redesigned the asset details page and added the following capabilities:

- Affinity grouping - Asset information is now intuitively organized.

- Patch versions - New Manage versions table to quickly view version details, add and delete a
  version, and change the lifecycle state for a version.

- Lifecycle states - View the lifecycle state of an asset.

- Last modified date - See when an asset was changed.

- Collapsible metadata - Hide and expand metadata such as version, last published, categories, and
  tags.

### New Features

  email address of a person to contact about the asset.

  request to both create an asset and set mutable asset data including tags, categories, custom
  fields, and documentation pages.

- For users who are not logged in, public portals display a disabled request access button with a
  tooltip explaining that the user must log in to make a request.

- Exchange prevents creating a category with an invalid value for the field `assetTypeRestrictions`.

## April 2019

### New Features

- Adding multiple tags to an asset is now easier. After a user types the tag and presses enter, a
  new tag is automatically started. (EXC-3431)

- Exchange events, such as the most recent asset details page visited in Exchange, are now shown in
  the Recent Items list in the common Anypoint Platform navigation bar. (EXC-3264)

- Users can now delete a draft of portal documentation. Previously users could only delete by
  editing the draft, removing all new edits, and publishing. When there were multiple changes in the
  draft, it could be difficult to tell which edits belonged to the draft and which to the old
  version. With the new option to delete a draft, users can have confidence that the right changes
  will be discarded automatically, preserving the original documentation content. (EXC-3116)

- Added information messages when trying to create a page with an invalid name in the Asset Detail
  Page to explain why the validation failed and how the user can make the page name valid.
  (EXC-3041)

- All policy URLs now have MuleSoft domains, so allowlists for API policies now require only
  MuleSoft URLs. No need to also add Amazon S3 URLs. (EXC-2680)

- Users can now automate the publishing process by using the Command Line Interface (CLI) to upload
  RAML and OAS specifications to Exchange. (EXC-2539)

### Fixed in this Release

- Exchange now generates the correct representation of mocking service URLs for OAS specifications.
  (EXC-3478)

- To prevent hackers from accessing the authorization token from the request header, the
  authorization token is no longer included in the request header in each request made with API
  Console. (EXC-3416)

- Enabled filtering by asset type in the public portal. (EXC-3400, EXC-3390)

- If the user creates a Terms and Conditions page to supplement their asset documentation page, the
  Terms and Conditions page is now visible at all times. (EXC-3383)

- Added `jpeg` to the list of supported extensions for portal resources (`bmp`, `gif`, `ico`, `jpe`,
  `jpeg`, `jpg`, `png`, `svg`, `tif`, `tiff`, `webp`). (EXC-3351)

- If the user selects the **API is behind firewall** option, navigates away, and returns, the
  selection is now remembered. (EXC-3335)

- Provided guardrails to prevent users from creating more than 50 pages in the documentation of a
  single asset. This prevents wasting unnecessary resources to support an unlimited number of pages.
  (EXC-3157)

- Prevented users from creating portal contents without an associated file when publishing API
  specifications. (EXC-2541)

## March 2019

### New Features

- Enable customers to use the Try It panel for API instances that are behind their firewall.
  (EXC-3117)

### Fixed in this Release

- Links to websites outside the MuleSoft Public Exchange no longer show a blank page. (EXC-3172)

- Dependency snippet in Public Exchange now shows up in focus, so users don’t have to scroll down
  and don’t fail to see the snippet dialog at the bottom of the page. (EXC-3166)

- Accurate warning and error displayed when the user has reached the Maximum Page limit of 10 pages
  per portal in Public Portal. (EXC-3054)

- There is no limit on the number of client applications or contracts visible to the user when the
  user tries to request access for an API or browses the client applications in the "My
  Applications" page. Previous limit was 200. (EXC-3017)

- Enable customers to add custom headers in the Try It panel in the Exchange Portal API Console.
  (EXC-3008)

- Maven dependencies for the test scope are no longer visible in the dependencies section in
  Exchange. (EXC-2624)

- Correct error message when trying to publish an OAS 3 specification, since OAS 3 is not supported.
  (EXC-2552)

- New error message reflects the correct information when an attempt is made to create a new asset
  with the same GroupID-AssetID-Version (GAV) as an asset deleted within the past 7 days. Error
  message changed from "Asset already exists. Choose another asset name or version." to "There is a
  deleted asset with the same version number. Try creating your new asset with a higher version
  number." (EXC-2484)

- Validate that a published WSDL has either a WSDL file or a URL for a WSDL file, and not both.
  (EXC-2354)

## February 2019

### New Features

- Syntax highlighting in asset description markdown content. (EXC-3226)

- Faster contextual navigation with clickable tags and categories in asset details page. By clicking
  on a tag or category, Exchange triggers a search of all of the assets that contain that tag or
  category. (EXC-3227)

- Easy drag and drop image upload on Exchange’s markdown editor. (EXC-3228)

### Fixed in this Release

- The organizationId field is mandatory when publishing assets through Exchange xAPIs. Previously
  not sending organizationId returned a misleading 404 (Not Found) error. Now not sending
  organizationId returns an accurate 400 (Bad Request) error. (EXC-3168)

- Public portals that use vanity domains to promote their company domain name can now render the API
  Console. API Console enables users to explore the API spec and try it out. (EXC-3143)

- When a user goes to edit mode from a page that does not exist in the draft, Exchange now opens the
  home page in edit mode without an error. (EXC-2992)

- Maven Facade now returns user-friendly and relevant error message text and code when internal
  services fail to validate a Mule asset. (EXC-2911)

- Previously exceeding the rate limit for the underlying authentication service returned a
  misleading 401 (Unauthorized) error. Now exceeding the rate limit for the underlying
  authentication service returns an accurate 429 (Too Many Requests) error. (EXC-2900)

- Exchange now prevents users from uploading compressed (zip) files whose uncompressed contents will
  exceed the maximum allowed size limit. Users will receive a 413 (Payload Too Large) HTTP error.
  (EXC-2527)

- Allow Cyrillic text in category names. (EXC-2461)

## 2.0.0

**July 29, 2017**

We are pleased to announce the general availability of the latest release of Anypoint Exchange. This
product enables Anypoint Platform users to publish and access Mule-related content within their own
organization increasing visibility and reuse.

### Compatibility

Exchange 2.0.0 is compatible with Anypoint Studio version 6.3 and later.

The new Anypoint Exchange 2 in Anypoint Platform offers a complete rework of Exchange with support
for OAS and RAML 1.0 specifications, an improved user interface, a new editor supporting both Visual
and Markdown text creation, and the ability to rate assets.

### New Features

Anypoint Exchange lets you:

- Store all integration assets in one place in Exchange, such as best practices, integration
  patterns, API fragments, API specifications, examples, templates, and connectors.

- Enrich portal content using the Visual editor and Markdown editor.

- Quickly upload Open API specifications (Swagger) in Exchange which automatically converts to RAML
  for use across the Anypoint toolset.

- Quickly upload WSDLs (SOAP APIs) in Exchange.

- Consume and reuse all existing MuleSoft public content in Anypoint Studio and Design Center.

- Collaborate with API owners and designers including the ability to comment and write reviews, ask
  questions, and provide feedback on each asset.

- Share an asset within a business group with users outside of the business group to drive cross
  business organization collaboration.

- Auto-generate a Mule 4.0 Design Center connector (using REST Connect) for any valid API
  specification for use within Design Center.

- View a list of dependencies (API Fragments) for any API specification.

- Version any asset published to Exchange.

- View Dependency Snippet for connectors for use in Maven, Gradle, SBT, and Ivy.

- Publish examples and templates using Studio 6.3 and later.

### Migration

Exchange 1.7 is still accessible and will remain available for 90 days (as of July 29). None of the
content on this old version of Exchange has been deleted. The URL for old Exchange is now
[https://anypoint.mulesoft.com/exchange1/](https://anypoint.mulesoft.com/exchange1/). Existing
customers with content on Private Exchange can also access the old Exchange using a link available
on the Exchange 2.0 site. You can migrate the content to Exchange 2.0 using
[migration instructions](../../exchange/migrate).

### Known Issues and Limitations

- EXC-1140: Unable to type anything below an image in the Visual editor. Switch to Markdown editor
  to continue editing.

- EXC-1253: Visual editor is not supported for use with Internet Explorer 11. Use the Markdown
  editor instead.

- Searching by tag at the user interface only works for the latest asset version.

- Admin user cannot delete reviews created by other users.

- Rating is not refreshed when a version is deleted.

- Unable to deprecate an asset.

- EXC-1522: Incorrect error message when a user without Exchange Contributor permission within a
  Business Group tries to create an asset.

- EXC-1269: In Firefox, when a token is expired and user tries to publish to exchange, it throws a
  403 error page. Clear cookies for Anypoint Platform and try again.

## May 2016

This new version of Anypoint Exchange includes new features & functionality for addressing the
viewing and publishing of artifacts across a hierarchical organization structure. Also within this
version of Exchange aligns with the Anypoint Platform Styles and use of the new Nav Bar.

### Features and Functionality

The following sections describe the new features in this release.

#### Visual Enhancements

Alignment with the Anypoint Platforms Styles and Integration with the latest Anypoint Platform
Navigation Bar.

#### Roles for Exchange

Besides the existing Organization Owner, Contributor and Administrator Roles, a separate Viewer role
was created.

#### New State and Flow Transition of an Artifact

To address the movement of an artifact across a hierarchical structure, Exchange now provides new
states for an artifact and also specific actions to be performed on them.

#### Business Groups

Business Groups are being incorporated in Exchange . This feature across with the Exchange Roles and
the new state transition flow of an artifact provides:

- Ability of Central IT (maybe the root organization) to create artifacts and make them available to
  all Lines of Businesses (business groups)

- Ability of Central IT to locate artifacts published in a business group and make it available to
  the rest of the business

- Ability of an LOB to publish artifacts for internal (to that business group) consumption

#### UI and UX Improvements

New Filters and actions now support the new Business Groups, Artifacts States, and Transition Flows
functionalities.

#### Edit Types Removal

Edit Terms only available on root Organization for Admin and Owner Organization

#### API Changes

Before this release, Exchange used an internal Organization ID in the API resource, but this
organization ID is replaced with the Access Management Organization ID to allow Business Groups. New
endpoints are being incorporated in Exchange to work with Business Groups. New permissions are
applied using the Business Groups hierarchy.

#### Avoid Losing User Data

When a session expires, Exchange prompts for credentials and completes the action. Exchange now
displays a warning when a user tries to leave the edit page if there are unsaved changes.

### Removed Features

- The object amount limitation for private tenants has been removed. The possibility to request to
  increase the object amount limit it’s already removed from the Exchange configuration in Anypoint
  Platform access management.

- The possibility to edit types was removed, all organizations now share the same types.

- The feature to edit terms can now only be enabled for users with Admin roles in root
  organizations.

### Architecture Changes

- Split UI from backend in different servers and all the related changes to fulfill this
  Architecture change.

- Update Node.js version to v4.

## Dec 2015

### Features and Functionality

This Anypoint Exchange release includes the following new features and functionality:

- WSDL Support: At the moment WSDL type does not have a Studio integration, however WSDLs can be
  added and managed via web UI.

- Visual enhancements such as new colors for item types and UX improvements.

- Auto-populated URI when creating new items.

- Automatically resizable description container when editing content.

- Firefox and Internet Explore 11 bugs fixed.

### Dec 2015 Known Limitations

The version of the exchange available with the on-premises installation of the Anypoint Platform
comes with an empty library of content, you must populate it with your own content.

## May 2015

### Features and Functionality

This Anypoint Exchange release includes the following new features and functionality:

- Ratings: All content has a rating associated to it. Users can rate only from Exchange in Anypoint
  Studio (Connectors need to be installed in Studio in order to rate them). Objects have their
  rating displayed only when they have two ratings or more.

- Author: Objects can have the author’s name and photo. This can be used for partners or community
  contributors. This section is hidden if not filled out.

- UI Refresh: Object type indicators have been improved . Text areas and button sizes have changed
  to improve readability

### Known Limitations

To access private content from Anypoint Studio, version 4.2.0 or newer must be used.

## May 2015 Private Cloud Edition

Version: 1.4.1

This Anypoint Exchange release includes these new features and functionality:

- Create and publish private content: Choose between a variety of content types (templates,
  examples, connectors, and more) to add, describe your asset, and publish it in your organization’s
  exchange. Only the people you choose may have access to create and publish new content.

- Search for content: Users within your organization can find the internally published content (as
  well as MuleSoft’s public content), increasing reuse and avoiding redundant work. Exchange Admins
  can customize search filters to make internal content easier to find.

### Known Issues

Accessing private content from Anypoint Studio requires version 4.2.0 or newer.

## February 2015

### Features and Functionality

This Anypoint Exchange release includes the following new features and functionality:

- Create and Publish private content: Choose between a variety of content types (templates,
  examples, connectors, etc) to add, describe your asset and publish it in your organization’s
  exchange. Only the people you choose may have access to create and publish new content.

- Search for Content: Users within your organization can find the internally published content (as
  well as MuleSoft’s public content), increasing the chance of reuse and avoiding redundant work.
  Exchange Admins can customize search filters to make internal content easier to find.

- Seamless Anypoint Studio Integration: Access your private content seamlessly from Anypoint Studio.
  You can open templates or install connectors by opening Anypoint Exchange from Studio and logging
  into your Anypoint Platform account.

### Known Limitations

To access private content from Anypoint Studio, version 4.2.0 or newer must be used.

# Omni Gateway Release Notes

> For the full documentation index, see: https://docs.mulesoft.com/llms.txt

Mulesoft Omni Gateway is an Envoy-based, ultrafast lightweight API gateway designed to manage and
secure APIs running anywhere. Built to seamlessly integrate with DevOps and CI/CD workflows, Omni
Gateway delivers the performance required for the most demanding applications and microservices
while providing enterprise security and manageability across any environment.

The following release notes are provided for Omni Gateway:

# Model Proxy Release Notes

> For the full documentation index, see: https://docs.mulesoft.com/llms.txt

These release notes reflect enhancements, changes, and bug fixes for model proxy.

In addition to these release notes, see:

- [Omni Gateway Release Notes](gateway-release-notes)

## August 6, 2026

### What’s New

- LLM Proxy is now renamed to model proxy.

- Model proxy now supports the Anthropic API format and native Anthropic models.

  See [Supported LLM Providers](../../general/model-proxy#supported-llm-providers).

## May 9, 2026

### What’s New

- Model proxy now supports Advanced Scale semantic services that use vector databases to store up to
  2000 utterance vectors per prompt topic.

  See
  [Configure an Advanced Scale Semantic Service](../../general/model-proxy-semantic-service#configure-an-advanced-scale-semantic-service).

- Agent Network now supports model proxies as Agent Broker LLM providers.

  See
  [Broker Project File References](../../agent-network/latest/af-project-files#llmproviders-section).

- Model proxy can now dynamically extract API Keys (such as OAuth 2.0 tokens) from incoming requests
  to support dynamic LLM provider authentication.

- Model proxies now support NVIDIA Nemotron models.

  See [Supported Models](../../general/model-proxy#brokers-section)

- Anypoint Monitoring now provides new dashboards for cost management.

## March 30, 2026

### What’s New

Model proxy provides a unified access layer for multiple Large Language Model (LLM) providers. Model
proxies are deployed to Omni Gateway to enable governance, intelligent routing, and cost management
for AI applications.

To learn more, see [Creating and Managing Model Proxies](../../general/model-proxy).

The MCP Payload Optimization policy reduces tool response token consumption using one or more
configurable methods: remove structural noise, trim oversized responses to match agent intent, or
compress repeated structures into TOON.

For configuration details, see
[MCP Payload Optimization Policy](../../../gateway/latest/policies-included-mcp-payload-optimization).

## July 11, 2026

### What’s New

- MCP Payload Optimization policy implementation version 1.2.0 is now supported by Omni Gateway.

- MCP Payload Optimization policy definition version 1.2.0 is now supported by Omni Gateway.

## July 10, 2026

### What’s New

- MCP Payload Optimization policy implementation version 1.0.2 is now supported by Omni Gateway.

- MCP Payload Optimization policy definition version 1.0.1 is now supported by Omni Gateway.

## August 10, 2026

### What’s New

- MCP Schema Validation policy definition and implementation version 1.2.0 is now supported by Omni
  Gateway.

- Added the **Tool Poisoning Detection** parameter, which detects tool-poisoning attacks against MCP
  `tools/list` responses by pinning the trusted tool set from the API’s Anypoint Exchange asset and
  comparing every backend `tools/list` response against it.

# MCP Support

> For the full documentation index, see: https://docs.mulesoft.com/llms.txt

The MCP Support policy adds MCP support to an Omni Gateway MCP server instance. This policy is
required for your MCP server instance to function properly.

For configuration details, see
[MCP Support Policy](../../../gateway/latest/policies-included-mcp-support).

## August 12, 2026

### What’s New

- MCP Support policy definition and implementation version 1.1.1 is now supported by Omni Gateway.

- Added the **Inject MCP Element Headers** parameter, which injects the MCP primitive as request
  headers for downstream policy use. The policy sets `x-ms-mcp-element-id` to the identifier and
  `x-ms-mcp-element-type` to the kind (`tool`, `prompt`, or `resource`).

## June 08, 2026

### What’s New

- MCP Support policy implementation version 1.0.9 is now supported by Omni Gateway.

## April 20, 2026

### What’s New

- MCP Support policy definition version 1.0.1 is now supported by Omni Gateway.

# MuleSoft Government Cloud Release Notes

> For the full documentation index, see: https://docs.mulesoft.com/llms.txt

These release notes describe updates to MuleSoft Government Cloud as from January 10, 2024.

## June 19, 2026

### What’s New

- MuleSoft Government Cloud now supports FIPS 140-3 compliance for Mule runtime engine 4.9.

  FIPS 140-3 replaces FIPS 140-2 as the supported cryptographic standard in Government Cloud. This
  update introduces support for Bouncy Castle 2.0.0 as the certified security provider, requires
  Java 17 or later, and mandates BCFKS keystore format and TLS 1.2 or TLS 1.3.

  For migration steps and configuration details, see
  [FIPS 140-3 Compliance Support](../../gov-cloud/gov-cloud-fips-140-3-support).

## April 8, 2025

### What’s New

- MuleSoft Government Cloud now supports Mule runtime engine version 4.9.3.

## May 8, 2024

### What’s New

- MuleSoft Government Cloud now supports Java 17.

  For more information, visit [Java Support](../../general/java-support).

## March 12, 2024

### What’s New

- MuleSoft Government Cloud now supports Mule runtime engine version 4.6.

  The March CloudHub 1.0 release introduces patches for Runtime versions 4.3.0 and 4.4.0 and Runtime
  4.6. This update is a breaking change as it enforces compliance with FIPS 140-2 on runtime
  versions 4.6, 4.4, and 4.3 for CloudHub applications within the MuleSoft Government Cloud.

  For more details about the impact of this update, check this article:

  - [GovCloud - March 2024 - Updates on FIPS Enforcement.](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=001186489&type=1)

## January 10, 2024

### What’s New

- Trusted domains allowlisting is now available in MuleSoft Government Cloud.

  For more information, visit
  [Allowing Trusted Domains for API Platform Proxies](../../gov-cloud/gov-cloud-security#allowing-trusted-domains-for-api-platform-proxies).

## See Also

- [Known Issues](https://help.salesforce.com/s/issues)

---
product: Release Notes
version: master
---

# Hyperforce Release Notes

> For the full documentation index, see: https://docs.mulesoft.com/llms.txt

These are the release notes for Salesforce Hyperforce (Hyperforce).

## August 19, 2026

### What’s New

- Hybrid Standalone Mule (HSA) is now available in all Hyperforce cloud control planes: US Cloud,
  Canada Cloud, EU Cloud, Japan Cloud, India Cloud, and Australia Cloud.  
  For more information, refer to [Features Supported](../../hyperforce/#features-supported).

- Monitoring for Hybrid Standalone Deployments in Anypoint Runtime Manager is now available in US

# IDP Release Notes

> For the full documentation index, see: https://docs.mulesoft.com/llms.txt

MuleSoft Intelligent Document Processing (IDP) enables you to read invoices, purchase orders, and
other unstructured or semi-structured documents and then analyze and refine the extracted content
using AI capabilities to create a structured response.

## July 10, 2026

## What’s New

- IDP now supports larger documents through the API.

  You can now process documents up to 150 pages and 15 MB when using the API execution endpoint.

  For complete file size limits, see [Quotas and Limits](../../idp/quotas-and-limits).

- You can now use Gemini 3.5 Flash and Claude Opus 4.6 to analyze your documents.

  For additional details on model support and performance, see
  [Supported Models](../../idp/supported-models).

## June 5, 2026

## What’s New

- You can now use Claude Sonnet 4.6 to analyze your documents.

  For additional details on model support and performance, see
  [Supported Models](../../idp/supported-models).

- You can now view published document action versions.

  Open earlier versions of your document actions to review their configuration without making
  changes. For additional details and instructions, see
  [View Published Document Action Versions](../../idp/publishing-document-actions#view-published-versions).

## May 5, 2026

## What’s New

- You can now use OpenAI GPT 5.1 and 5.2 to analyze your documents.

  For additional details on model support and performance, see
  [Supported Models](../../idp/supported-models).

- You can now search and filter document actions in the **Document Actions** page.

## April 2, 2026

## What’s New

- Updated OpenAI model names.

  - Einstein OpenAI GPT-4o Mini 0718 is now Einstein OpenAI GPT-4o Mini.

  - Einstein OpenAI GPT-4o 0806 is now Einstein OpenAI GPT-4o.

## March 20, 2026

## What’s New

- Removed Gemini 3 model support.

  This feature isn’t quite ready, so we’re removing it for now. We’ll let you know when it’s back
  up.

## March 10, 2026

## What’s New

- You can now enable location callouts in Generic document actions with customized schemas.

  For additional details about supported models and limitations, see
  [Configure Document Action Settings](../../idp/creating-document-actions#document-action-settings)

- You can now select Google’s GEMINI-3.0 Flash (Beta) model to analyze your documents.

  For additional usage details and considerations about this model, see
  [Supported Models](../../idp/supported-models)

## October 29, 2025

## What’s New

- You can now select Google’s GEMINI-2.5 Flash model to analyze your documents.

## June 3, 2025

## What’s New

- You can now rotate documents in the document action builder preview and review task preview.

  The rotation is for visual assistance and does not modify the original file.

## Fixed Issues

<table><colgroup><col> <col></colgroup><thead><tr><th>Issue Resolution</th><th>ID</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><div><div><p>For the <strong>emails</strong> field in Purchase Order and Invoice actions, IDP now returns <code>null</code> instead of an empty array <code>[]</code> in the execution response after reviewing the associated task.</p></div></div></td><td><div><div><p>W-17330495</p></div></div></td></tr></tbody></table>

## May 20, 2025

## What’s New

- You can now **Submit** review tasks without having to scroll to the end of the fields list,
  improving accessibility.

## May 8, 2025

## What’s New

- You can now enable image recognition in your document actions.

  To enable this feature, see
  [Configure Document Action Settings](../../idp/analyzing-documents-with-einstein#settings).

- You can now select Google’s GEMINI-2.0 Flash 001 model to analyze your documents.

  To select the model to use, see
  [Configure Document Action Settings](../../idp/analyzing-documents-with-einstein#settings).

  For additional information about supported models, see
  [Supported Models](../../idp/supported-models)

- Einstein prompts now support up to 128,000 input tokens per request.

  For additional details about token consumption, see
  [Token Usage and Estimation](../../idp/quotas-and-limits#tokens).

- Data retention policies are updated:

  - For all successful executions, IDP now retains the data for 24 hours.

  - IDP now retains any incomplete tasks for 30 days.

## February 5, 2025

## What’s New

- You can now analyze any type of document and fully customize the output structure by creating a
  Generic document action and enabling **Customize Schema**.

  For more information, see
  [Analyzing Documents With Custom User-Defined Schemas](../../idp/analyzing-documents-with-einstein).

  - Generic document actions now support using non-English characters for prompt instructions when
    **Customize Schema** is enabled.

- New document actions now support the `GPT-4o (gpt-4o-2024-08-06)` and
  `GPT-4o Mini (gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18)` LLM Models.

- New document actions now support masking any personally identifiable information from your
  documents before sending it to the predictive model.

- The API portal documentation for IDP assets published to Exchange now includes the `valueOnly`
  query parameter.

- You can now upload files in Base64 encoding for versioned action executions.

  For an example API call, see
  [Upload a Base64-encoded File](../../idp/automate-document-processing-with-the-idp-api#upload-base64-file).

- IDP can now detect signatures in document actions that use Einstein.

## November 7, 2024

> uninstall script and then re-install the Anypoint Monitoring agent.

regions.

## March 5, 2026

**Version 3.2.14.0**

### What’s New

The 3.x version of the Anypoint Monitoring agent introduces:

- Support for configuring the OTel collector’s internal telemetry log level during installation
  using the `-l` parameter. This feature is available on supported Linux and Windows operating
  systems. Accepted values are `info` (default), `debug`, `warn`, `error`, and `off`.

  Example (Linux): `# am/bin/install -l error`

- Support for enabling tracing during installation using the `-g` parameter. This feature is
  available on supported Linux and Windows operating systems. Sets the port for tracing data that
  comes from Mule runtime (see
  [OpenTelemetry Support in Mule Runtime](../../mule-runtime/latest/otel-support)). This parameter
  is disabled by default.

  Example (Linux): `# am/bin/install -g 4317`

For information about the agent, see
[Setting Up Monitoring for Hybrid Deployments](../../monitoring/am-installing).

## February 10, 2026

**Version 3.2.12.5**

### What’s New

The 3.x version of the Anypoint Monitoring agent introduces:

- Support for multiple installations of the agent to a single Linux host

- Updated service templates to support the new port configuration

This release also includes a security update.

  commons-lang3 library. (SE-18329)

- You could not install Anypoint Monitoring on hot-fix runtimes.

- The enhanced API metrics were not sent to Anypoint Monitoring.

### Version 2.3.0.0 July 20, 2020

This release contains the following fixed issues:

- Fixed an issue in which metrics were not recorded for a period of time after restarting app on UI
  in Server Group. (SE-16753)

- Fixed an issue in which `filebeat.exe` locked log files, which prevented log files from being
  rotated. (SE-16160)

- Added support for `RollingRandomAccessFileAppender` for Log4j. (SE-16003)

- Fixed an issue in which the **Application Process CPU Load** graph displayed incorrect values.
  (SE-15911)

### Version 2.2.3.0 April 27, 2020

This release contains the following fixed issues:

- Added support for Anypoint Visualizer properties configured from Runtime Manager Properties tab
  for Mule 4. (SE-14999)

- Fixed the issue of not picking the modification for property values unless Mule Runtime is
  restarted. (SE-15543)

### Version 2.2.2.0 April 6, 2020

This release includes the following update:

Header injection for Anypoint Visualizer is enabled by default for Mule 4.

This release contains the following fixed issues:

- Fixed a download connection error when the server is behind a proxy. (SE-15234)

- Fixed an error about am module directory not found. (SE-15374)

### Version 2.2.1.0 February 10, 2020

This release contains the following fixed issues:

- On Mule 4.x, JMX Publisher stopped creating JVM metrics after running for some time. (SE-14730)

  - This fix requires Runtime Manager agent 2.4.5+.

- Outbound metrics erroneously included some internal calls. (SE-14055)

- Some outbound metrics showed an incorrect response time of 24 hours. (SE-13973)

- Improved endpoint normalization. (SE-12965)

- Fixed error on deleting file after copy. (SE-14578)

### Version 2.2.0.0 December 19, 2019

This release contains the following fixed issues:

- Metric logs stopped updating JVM and OS metrics on deployment failure. (SE-13917)

- The Anypoint Monitoring agent was blocking threads. (SE-14121)

### Version 2.1.7.0 August 28, 2019

This release contains the following fixed issues:

- Anypoint Visualizer is not showing inbound connections. (SE-12476)

- Anypoint Monitoring `am` folder is recreated after uninstall. (SE-12769)

- Inbound Metrics are missing for app in Anypoint Monitoring. (SE-12832)

### Version 2.1.6.0 August 6, 2019

This release contains the following fixed issues:

- Log forwarding does not work for newly deployed app without Mule runtime restart. (SE-12605)

- Uninstall script not removing files properly. (SE-12599)

- No infrastructure metrics for certain applications. (SE-12473)

- Analytics collector doesn’t allow to access message. (SE-12446)

### Version 2.1.5.0 July 15, 2019

This release includes the following update:

- Install script no longer requires `-s <server-id>` parameter.

This release contains the following fixed issue:

- Log forwarding does not work with Anypoint Monitoring agent 2.1.4.0 in hybrid runtime. (SE-12410)

### Version 2.1.4.0 June 7, 2019

This release contains the following fixed issue:

- High thread count in a clustered environment (SE-11772)

### Version 2.1.2.0 May 17, 2019

This release includes the following updates:

- Added support for Mule 4.2.x and Runtime Manager agent 2.3.x.

- Added support for Filebeat restart if configuration or certificates have changed.

This release includes the following fixed issues:

- Anypoint Monitoring with Multicast Cluster Setup (SE-11657)

- Layer when deploying app from RM (SE-10374)

- Fix NPE reported in Mule log at startup (SE-11483)

- Some inbound request failures are not taken into account in Monitoring dashboards. (SE-10544)

### Version 2.1.0.0 March 26, 2019

or from the Anypoint Monitoring **Settings > Hybrid** page.

## July 24, 2026

Anypoint Monitoring enhances the Log Search experience across all Anypoint Platform clouds.

### What’s New

[Log Search](../../monitoring/logs-search-hf) now supports:

- Viewing the top five values in each field

- Adding or removing the field from the **Results** table

- Filtering by any of the displayed values or, if the field contains more than five values, creating
  a search filter using **See More**

On EU and US Clouds, Log Search has fully rolled out. The previous Log Search experience is no
longer available from **Classic Monitoring** in Anypoint Monitoring.

## July 10, 2026

On US and EU Clouds, Anypoint Monitoring updates basic alerts.

### What’s New

This update brings [Alerts](../../monitoring/alerts-hf) into alignment on all clouds.

## June 30, 2026

Anypoint Monitoring releases new and updated features in all clouds.

### What’s New

Anypoint Monitoring continues to bring features into alignment globally.

### What’s New

Anypoint Insights dashboards introduce new charts and visualizations of metrics in EU, US, Japan
(JP), and Canada (CA) cloud instances of Anypoint Platform. These app and API metrics bring Anypoint
Insights dashboards into near parity with metrics displayed through the built-in dashboards in
Anypoint Monitoring.

- [New API Metrics in Anypoint Insights](#api-visualizations)

To compare built-in dashboard charts and visualizations with those now in Anypoint Insights, see
[API Chart Mapping](../../monitoring/api-dashboard#api-chart-parity) and
[App Chart Mapping](../../monitoring/app-dashboards#app-chart-parity).

For descriptions of Anypoint Insights charts and visualizations in app and API details pages, see:

- [**Application Details**](../../monitoring/anypoint-insights#entity-metrics-apps) in Anypoint
  Insights

- [**API Details**](../../monitoring/anypoint-insights#entity-metrics-apis) in Anypoint Insights

### New Application Metrics in Anypoint Insights

Anypoint Insights adds charts and visualizations of application metrics in **Application Details**
tabs:

- App **Overview** tab:

  - No new charts or visualizations in this release

- App **Request** tab:

  - **Inbound - Maximum Response Time by Endpoint**

  - **Request Volume by Protocol**

  - **Request Volume by HTTP Endpoint**

  - **Outbound Request Volume by Port**

  - **Outbound Request Volume by Remote Host**

  - **Outbound Request Latency**

  - **Outbound Request Volume by Operation**

    For more information, see
    [Request Metrics for a Mule Application](../../monitoring/anypoint-insights#entity-metrics-app-requests).

- App **Errors** tab:

  - **Inbound - Response Time by Endpoint**, **Outbound - Response Time by Endpoint**

  - **Inbound - Request Count by Endpoint**, **Outbound - Request Count by Endpoint**

  - **Failed Mule Messages**

    For more information, see
    [Error Metrics for a Mule Application](../../monitoring/anypoint-insights#entity-metrics-app-errors).

- App **Flows** tab (new in this release):

  - **Inbound - Response Time by Flow**, **Outbound - Response Time by Flow**

  - **Inbound - Requests by Flow**, **Outbound - Requests by Flow**

  - **Inbound - Response Time by Flow**, **Outbound - Response Time by Flow**

  - **Inbound - Requests by Flow**, **Outbound - Requests by Flow**

  - **Failures by Flow**

    For more information, see
    [Flow Metrics for a Mule Application](../../monitoring/anypoint-insights#entity-metrics-app-flows).

- App **Connectors** tab (new in this release):

  - **Connector Message Volume**

  - **Response Time by Connector**

  - **Salesforce Requests**, **Salesforce Response Time**, **Salesforce Failures**

  - **Database Requests**, **Database Response Time**, **Database Failures**

  - **HTTP Requests**, **HTTP Response Time**, **HTTP Failures**

  - **Web Service Requests**, **Web Service Response Time**, **Web Service Failures**

  - **FTP Requests**, **FTP Response Time**, **FTP Failures**

  - **SFTP Requests**, **SFTP Response Time**, **SFTP Failures**

  - **SMTP Requests**, **SMTP Response Time**, **SMTP Failures**

  - **Object Store Requests**, **Object Store Response Time**, **Object Store Failures**

  - **Anypoint MQ Operations - Inbound**, **Anypoint MQ Response Time - Inbound**, **Anypoint MQ
    Failures - Inbound**

  - **Anypoint MQ Operations - Outbound**, **Anypoint MQ Response Time - Outbound**, **Anypoint MQ
    Failures - Outbound**

  - **Other Connector Requests**, **Other Connector Response Time**, **Other Connector Failures**

    For more information, see
    [Connector Metrics for a Mule Application](../../monitoring/anypoint-insights#entity-metrics-app-connectors).

- App **JVM** tab:

  - **Classes Loaded**, **Classes Loaded Total**, **Classes Unloaded**

  - **JVM Uptime**

  - **Par Eden Space** , **G1 Eden Space**

  - **Par Survivor Space**, **G1 Survivor Space**

  - **Metaspace**

  - **Compressed Class Space**

  - **JVM Memory Code Cache**, **Code Cache**

  - **Tenured Gen**, **G1 Old Gen**

    For more information, see
    [JVM Metrics for a Mule Application](../../monitoring/anypoint-insights#entity-metrics-app-jvm).

- App **Custom Metrics** tab:

  Monitor apps that use your organization’s custom metrics for a Mule application. Adjust settings
  of the charts that use your custom metrics.

  The **Custom Metrics** tab for an application appears in Anypoint Insights only if your
  organization has the Anypoint Integration Advanced package or a Titanium subscription to Anypoint
  Platform and the application you selected from Anypoint Insights is running on a supported version
  of Mule.

  For more information, see
  [Custom Metrics for a Mule Application](../../monitoring/anypoint-insights#entity-metrics-app-custom-metrics).

## March 23, 2026

### What’s New

Use Integration Intelligence to monitor, analyze, and troubleshoot your MuleSoft telemetry data
directly in the Salesforce ecosystem and unlock the analytics engine for modern integration.
Integration Intelligence, which is now generally available in the US and EU cloud regions only,
includes enhancements since the beta release in November 2025:

- Create custom dashboards in Integration Intelligence to monitor metrics for your Mule apps and
  APIs. Pinpoint inefficiencies, benchmark performance, and drive smarter optimization decisions.

- Create custom visualizations from metrics belonging to the MuleSoft semantic model.

- View app and API performance metrics in the built-in dashboards.

- Select a time range for data displayed in the built-in dashboards and logs.

- Get data from more deployment types (in addition to CloudHub 2.0 and Runtime Fabric):

  - CloudHub (dashboard metrics only)

- Set up Integration Intelligence in a _default_ data space (not a custom data space at this time).

Unsupported in this release:

- Canada and Japan cloud regions

- CloudHub deployments for logs

- Flex Gateway visualizations for dashboards

- Agentic assets (brokers, agents, and MCP servers)

- Custom data spaces when setting up Integration Intelligence

See [Integration Intelligence](../../monitoring/integration-intelligence).

## December 7, 2021

## What’s New

- In **Custom Dashboards**, advanced mode has two new metrics:

  - `disk_stats`

  - `operatingsystem`

## November 9, 2021

## What’s New

- The world map chart is now available for built-in dashboards with enhanced API metrics.  
  In the **Client Application** section, the **Requests by Location** chart displays a world map
  that shows the number of requests per geographic location.

## September 13, 2021

## What’s New

- Anypoint Monitoring now has two product-specific permissions: Anypoint Monitoring Viewer and
  Anypoint Monitoring Administrator.

  - The Anypoint Monitoring Viewer permission enables a user only to view assets in Anypoint
    Monitoring.

  - The Anypoint Monitoring Administrator permission enables a user to view, create, modify, and
    delete assets in Anypoint Monitoring.

- The **Overview** section of built-in API dashboards for enhanced metrics has two new charts. The
  **Total 4xx Errors** and **Total 5xx Errors** charts show the sum of all 400- and 500-errors
  respectively.

## June 16, 2021

### Enhancements

- Reports have a new column that specifies the `target name`, or location where the target is
  deployed, of the resource for which you are viewing a report.

- The following charts were renamed:

  - **Inbound - Total Requests by Endpoint** is now **Inbound - Total Requests by HTTP Endpoint**.

  - **Outbound - Total Requests by Endpoint** is now **Outbound - Total Requests by HTTP Endpoint**.

- Previously, in the **Custom Dashboards** API panel, APIs that did not support enhanced metrics did
  not appear. For enhanced usability, these APIs now appear in the API panel but are disabled.

- The `${timestamp}` variable is now available in alert email templates.

### Fixed Issues

- If you had previously chosen an environment when you accessed the **Reports** page, an error
  occurred when you tried to click **View**.

- When you accessed the **Custom Dashboards** page and clicked **Configure**, the **Save** button
  appeared before you made any changes.

- In **Custom Dashboards**, when you selected everything for an API Panel and changed to API
  Analytics Panel (deprecated), an error occured and your selections remained in each field. Because
  the metrics between API panels are different, your selections are now reset when you switch
  between API panel types.

- Fixed an issue related to the `group by` for the **Inbound - HTTP Endpoints** chart.

- Fixed an issue in which the **Inbound - Total Requests by HTTP Endpoint** and **Outbound - Total
  Requests by HTTP Endpoint** charts had empty cells. (SE-20663)

- In the **Built-in Dashboards** page, when you viewed an API that supported both basic and enhanced
  metrics and then clicked the **Switch to basic metrics** link, the **Switch to basic metrics**
  link did not work. (SE-19796)

- When you created a server alert, servers did not load automatically.

- When you created an API panel in **Custom Dashboards**, if you selected everything, changed to
  advanced mode, and then switched back to simple mode, API selector tried to load indefinitely.

- In **Custom Dashboards**, if you had two Runtime Fabric apps available that had the same name,
  there was an issue selecting the second one. (SE-20637)

- When you used Safari to access built-in dashboards, the date picker did not work properly.
  (SE-20203)

- When you used a link to **Log Search** that was shared by another user in the same organization,
  an error occurred if the query parameter in the URL was encoded:
  `The sharer organization is not the same as the active one.` You can now access log search after
  encoding query parameters in URLs. (SE-20282)

- When you had multiple hybrid apps deployed to the same server, created a custom dashboard, and
  then selected the second app out of the hybrid apps deployed to that server as the **Resource**,
  your selection changed to the first app deployed to that server whenever you tried to reconfigure
  the panel. (SE-20453)

## March 16, 2021

### Enhancements

- Basic alerts now support email templates. You can populate the subject and message body of basic
  alert emails to include variables for the alert metric, condition, severity, and more. For a
  complete list of available variables, refer to the
  [basic alerts documentation](../../monitoring/alerts-hf#alert-variables).

- The **Alerts** page now sorts alerts by the most recently updated.

- When you use the Log Search feature, the logs that appear alongside the target log entry now load
  more quickly. SE-17024

- The **Connector Message Volume** chart tooltip has been enhanced to read **Number of outbound
  requests, grouped by connector type**.

- The following charts have been renamed:

  - **Inbound - Response Time by Endpoint** is now **Inbound - Response Time by HTTP Endpoint**.

  - **Inbound - Endpoints** is now **Inbound - HTTP Endpoints**.

  - **Outbound - Ports** is now **Outbound - HTTP Ports**.

  - **Outbound - Protocols** is now **Outbound - HTTP Protocols**.  
    SE-18756, SE-18909

- The following charts include enhanced queries for more accurate metrics reporting:

  - Inbound - Response Time by HTTP Endpoint

  - Inbound - HTTP Endpoints

  - Outbound - HTTP Ports

  - Outbound - HTTP Protocols

  - Outbound - Operations  
    SE-18756, SE-18909

### Fixed Issues

- Fixed an issue related to timeouts while searching for surrounding logs. SE-17024

- Fixed an issue in which multiline logs in log searches resulted in multiple events. SE-18091

- In basic mode of custom dashboards for hybrid apps, you could not select applications other than
  the first application that appeared when you accessed the resource selector. SE-19604

- Fixed an issue related to ordering applications by name when you clicked the **Application Name**
  column in reports.

- Fixed an issue related to deleting alerts while filters were enabled.

## January 27, 2021

### Enhancements

- Basic and advanced alerts now include a selection for user-defined severity. Note that when you
  modify existing alerts, you must assign a severity to that alert before you can save changes.

- You can now sort and filter alerts by severity in the **Alerts** page.

- When you create an alert and begin entering a value in the **Recipients** field, user emails
  associated with your organization that match the value you entered appear.

### Fixed Issues

- When you had apps with the same name deployed to multiple Anypoint Runtime Fabric clusters:

  - Regardless of which instance of the app you selected, the same one always appeared.

  - The metrics associated with that app were combined.

  To accommodate this fix, built-in dashboard URLs have been enhanced to use the app’s ID to
  differentiate between instances of deployed apps. If you reload the page using the previous URL,
  the page will not load. (SE-19017)

- The Inbound - Response Time by Flow chart erroneously displayed the same value for average,
  minimum, and maximum columns. (SE-19048)

- The **Raw Data** page did not load for some Runtime Fabric users. (SE-18626, SE-19093)

- The data for Inbound - Requests by Flow and Inbound - Response Time by Flow charts were swapped.
  (SE-18786, SE-19048)

- In built-in API analytics charts, the following charts erroneously showed sums, instead of
  averages:

  - Average Response Time

  - Requests by Performance

  - Slow Requests  
    (SE-17969)

- General bug fixes and security enhancements.

Your environment now loads correctly during custom dashboard creation.

## November 12, 2020

### Fixed Issues

- If you had the same API deployed in two or more environments, the corresponding API widget label
  continued to show the first environment the API instance was deployed to, even after saving and
  reconfiguring the graph.

- Infinite scrolling did not work in the list of alerts.

- When using Anypoint Monitoring, the **Sign Out** button did not log you out of Anypoint Platform.

- When you clicked a link in an alert email, some redirects did not work as expected. The link in
  the alert email now directs you to an error page if that link goes to:

  - A dashboard that is in a different organization than the current active organization.

available.

### Fixed Issues

- When you searched for an API instance or version, the search feature did not suggest results based
  on the version.

- When selecting assets to view in built-in dashboards, the supported runtime versions tooltip
  erroneously stated `Version 3.8.7-AM is supported for log search only`. All -AM runtime versions
  are deprecated.

- In **Built-in Dashboards**, the **Inbound - Maximum Response Time** chart used the wrong query to
  populate the chart.

### New Feature

> [!NOTE] This feature is currently available only for certain customers.

You can now quickly and seamlessly create basic alerts for app and server metrics.

Basic alerts are available for the following metrics for servers or Mule apps:

- For on-premises servers and CloudHub apps:

  - Memory utilization

  - Thread count

- For on-premises, Runtime Fabric, and CloudHub apps:

  - Message error count

  - Message response time

## May 20, 2020

### New Feature

You can now access the Anypoint Visualizer Troubleshooting visualization for an app in the
**Application Network** section of the **Built-In Dashboards** page in Anypoint Monitoring. The
**Application Network** section enables you to view direct callers and callees for a single app for
the most recent seven days.

[download this API](https://anypoint.mulesoft.com/exchange/portals/anypoint-platform/f1e97bc6-315a-4490-82a7-23abe036327a.anypoint-platform/anypoint-monitoring-archive-api/)
using Anypoint Exchange. This API is available only for users who have a Titanium subscription.

## June 12, 2019

Anypoint Monitoring support for Mule 3.9.x-AM and Mule 4.x-AM is being deprecated.

Update your applications to run on Mule versions 3.9.x and 4.x for better functionality and improved
performance, and to receive the latest patch updates as soon as they are available.

If you currently have Anypoint Monitoring enabled for applications running Mule 3.9.x-AM or 4.x-AM,
monitoring continues to work, but you will not receive important patch updates.

For information about setting the runtime version for your Mule app and enabling monitoring, see
[Configure and Enable Anypoint Monitoring for Mule Apps](../../monitoring/configure-monitoring-cloudhub).
